emerging_technology: Text-to-image diffusion models, with latent diffusion as the reference architecture
intended_application: Generate internal advertising concept images and mood boards for homeware campaigns; final product photographs and advertising copy remain separately authored and checked.
organization: A hypothetical small U.S. online homeware retailer with two marketing employees. The owner approves existing creative concepts; no AI evaluation sponsor, accountable pilot lead or ongoing operating owner has been designated.
industry_sector: Consumer homeware retail and digital marketing
business_need: Determine whether the organization can plan, authorize, staff and govern a bounded comparison of AI-assisted INTERNAL campaign concept boards against its current manual/designer workflow; no measured benefit is assumed.
users_stakeholders: Two marketing employees, the store owner, a freelance designer, a possible future review owner, and customers who may see only separately approved final materials.
capabilities_constraints: Strengths: two employees already edit visual content and use a product catalogue for references; the owner approves concepts; manual boards and a freelance designer remain available. Unknown: approved staff-hour allocation, AI-specific skill/training, staff attitudes, named evaluation coordinator, person responsible for product-detail fidelity review, vendor and input-use terms, approved budget, and repeatable acceptance measures. There is no ML team; buying or training a model is not proposed.
risk_consequence_context: Internal concept images may be discarded and are never auto-published. Risk still includes misrepresented product details, confidentiality or input-use terms, review burden, team opportunity cost and adoption into workflows without accountable oversight.
management_question: Even if the Assignment 6 conditional bounded experiment is strategically sensible, can this two-person marketing organization absorb, govern, staff and sustain the internal concept-board application? What readiness evidence, owner and prioritized changes are required before a trial is authorized?
time_horizon: Six-week readiness review and possible trial-authorization decision, not a deadline to deploy or proof of business value.
additional_context:
ASSIGNMENT 7 ORGANIZATIONAL READINESS FACTS (all hypothetical scenario assumptions, not real fieldwork): There is no confirmed AI-specific training, staff availability, signed tool rights, image accuracy review checklist or named long-term operator. The owner approves existing concepts but has NOT explicitly sponsored an AI trial. The manual workflow is retained. Any authorization and adoption decision remain separate from preparing a proposal. The previous Assignment 6 agent conditionally favored PREPARING a bounded internal comparison, not immediate trial execution or rollout. Missing facts must be marked unknown, not assumed absent or sufficient. The highest-stakes interview question is who can own and staff the pilot and review work without impairing ongoing marketing activity.
